Shawn Christopher Respert was born on February 6, 1972.
Shawn Respert is an American professional basketball coach and former player.
Respert attended Bishop Borgess High School.
Respert played college basketball at Michigan State.
Respert and Eric Snow formed one of the nation's most prolific backcourt tandems for Jud Heathcote's Spartans.
Respert was the team's leading scorer all four seasons at Michigan State.
Respert finished his career second all-time in scoring among Big Ten players with 2,531 points (trailing only Calbert Cheaney).
Respert was first in Big Ten games with 1,545 points scored.
Respert capped a brilliant career by being named a unanimous first team All-American and Big Ten Player of the Year.
Respert had a 25.6 scoring average during his 1994–95 senior season.
Respert left East Lansing as the Spartans' all-time leading scorer.
Respert began the tradition of outgoing seniors kissing the logo at center court during their final home game.
Respert was selected by the Portland Trail Blazers in the 1st round, with the 8th overall pick, of the 1995 NBA draft.
The Blazers traded Respert's NBA rights to the Milwaukee Bucks for the rights to Gary Trent and a first-round pick.
Respert was traded to Toronto in his second year.
Respert scored 5.6 points per game during his time with Toronto.
Respert played briefly in Dallas the next season.
Respert had a second stint with the Raptors.
Respert finished his career in Phoenix during the 1998–99 season.
Respert was under contract with Los Angeles Lakers for a brief period in October 2000 but was waived before playing in any NBA games for them.
In his NBA career, Respert played in 172 games and scored a total of 851 points on averages of 4.9 points per game in 13.7 minutes per game.
Respert played professionally in Italy for Adecco Milano from 1999 to 2000.
Respert played professionally in Italy for Fillattice Imola from 2001 to 2002.
Respert played professionally in Poland for Spójnia Stargard Szczeciński from 2002 to 2003.
Respert had stomach cancer but did not admit it until 2005.
Respert started being bothered with stomach cramps towards the end of his rookie season.
Respert noticed a lump below his belly button even after changing his diet.
Respert was diagnosed with cancer after undergoing a series of tests at Milwaukee's St. Joseph Regional Medical Center in May 1996.
Respert underwent daily radiation therapy for three consecutive months, losing twenty pounds in the process.
Only the Bucks' trainers, doctors, coach Mike Dunleavy, Sr., and Michigan State backcourt partner Eric Snow knew about this treatment.
Respert only told a select few; not even his family and girlfriend knew.
Respert became a volunteer coach at Prairie View A&M in Texas in 2004.
In early 2005, Respert was hired to be director of basketball operations at Rice University for 21⁄2 years.
Respert then spent two years as the director of player development of the NBA's minor league, the NBA Development League.
In September 2008, Respert was hired by the Houston Rockets as the director of player programs.
On December 6, 2011, Respert was hired by the Minnesota Timberwolves as a player development coach.
Respert was named an assistant coach by the Memphis Grizzlies in September 2013.
Respert moved to the Chicago Bulls as a director of player development in 2018.
Respert's tenure with the Bulls lasted until the end of the 2019–20 season when his contract expired.
